newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia INCO says 9-month net down.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia INCO says 9-month net down.

text.p: PT International Nickel Indonesia (INCO) said on Thursday net earnings in the first nine months fell from the same period last year because of lower world nickel prices and higher costs of production.
It said net profit in the nine months ending September declined to $54 million, or 22 cents a share, from $70.6 million, or 28 cents a share, in the corresponding period last year.

INCO, majority owned by Inco Ltd of Canada, said net earnings for the third quarter of 1996 were $14.5 million, or six cents per share, against $31.6 million, or 12 cents a shar,e in the same period last year.

"The decrease in net earnings in the third quarter and first nine months of 1996, relative to the corresponding 1995 periods, principally reflected lower nickel price realisations, lower deliveries and inccreased unit production costs," it said.
INCO said its net realised price for nickel in matte averaged $2.63 per pound in the third quarter of 1996, compared with $3.03 per pound in the same 1995 period.
It said the average price for the first nine months of 1996 was $2.77 per pound against $2.95 in 1995.
The selling price of nickel in matte, an intermediate product which is sold under long-term contract, is determined by a formula based upon the London Metal Exchange cash price for nickel, it said.
INCO said production for the third quarter of 1996 was 23.7 million pounds against 23.4 million in the same 1995 period.
INCO said increased unit production costs in the third quarter of 1996 compared with 1995 were primarily due to higher prices for oil and supplies.
It also said that property losses arising from a blast in a furnace in September would be covered by insurance, although production shortfalls were significant.
"It is expected that about six million pounds of nickel in matte production will be lost in 1996 due to the eruption and repair of furnace three," INCO said.
Furnace three is one of the firm's three electric furnaces.
INCO said property damage resulting from the explosion was expected to be covered by insurance, subject to a minor deductible.
It said repairs to furnace three were continuing on schedule and it was expected to be back on line in December this year and at full production in January 1997.
